 Canadiens @ Hurricanes: Preview and Game Thread
 by Bob Wage Nov 19, 2026, 3:40 AM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 HELSINKI, FINLAND - NOVEMBER 14: Andrei Svechnikov #37 of the Carolina Hurricanes celebrates his power play goal against the Seattle Kraken during the second period of the 2026 Global Series game at Veikkaus Arena on November 14, 2026 in Helsinki, Finland. (Photo by Brian Babineau/NHLI via Getty Images) NHLI via Getty Images After an incredibly successful NHL Global Series Finland, the Carolina Hurricanes (16-3-2) are back home and will take on the Montreal Canadiens (12-5-4) on Thursday night at the Lenovo Center. Game time is 7 P.M.
 This is a big game for more than one reason as the home team is holding their annual “Hockey Fights Cancer” game. Several players met with kids at UNC Children’s Hospital this week and there are several fundraising functions going on. For more information, check out the following link.
 https://www.nhl.com/hurricanes/news/hurricanes-to-hold-hockey-fights-cancer-game-thursday-november-19 
 Carolina’s record of 16-3-2 for the season so far closely matches how they finished last season with a 16-3-0 last postseason, giving them a record of 32-6-2 in their last 40 games played. Not too shabby!
 The Canes have won four in a row and have a 8-1-1 record in their last 10 games.
 The Habs are coming off a win against the Devils Wednesday night. They are 6-2-2 in their last 10.
 Sebastian Aho is having himself a season so far and leads the team with 29 points in his 21 games. Andrei Svechnikov is next with 21 points and Jackson Blake is right there, also with 21 points.
 Carolina is second in league scoring with 87 goals but is number one in goal differential with a plus 40.
 The home team will not hold a morning skate, but they have skated the following lines during the last two practices.
 It looks like Pyotr Kochetkov will return between the pipes, but that is unconfirmed. Eric Robinson draws back in replacing Jesperi Kotkaniemi. We will see how long that lasts.
 The Habs are led by Lane Hutson and Cole Caufield with 22 points and 19 points respectively in their 22 games. Nick Suzuki has returned from an injury and he has notched 18 points in 16 games.
 Watch the game locally on Prime Video, Fubo, or Spectrum. Listen via 99.9 The Fan.
